messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: Model averaging in Distance
parts:
Douglas:

The graphical user interface to Distance limits the number of model
definitions to 5. However, if you look at the Log window, you can see a
set of commands in the MCDS command language like this:

Estimate;
Distance;
Density=All;
Encounter=All;
Detection=All;
Size=All;
Estimator /Key=HN /Adjust=CO /Criterion=AIC;
Estimator /Key=HN /Adjust=PO /Criterion=AIC;
Estimator /Key=UN /Adjust=PO /Criterion=AIC;
Estimator /Key=HA /Adjust=PO /Criterion=AIC;
Estimator /Key=HA /Adjust=CO /Criterion=AIC;
Monotone=Strict;
Pick=AIC;

These lines are created by the graphical interface. If you need more
models, you can alter the commands (specifying more models) run MCDS
from the command line of your operating system. This process, if you
are adept at working directly with the operating system from the command
line, is explained in the Users Guide appendix entitled: MCDS Engine
Reference.

Fundamentally you will be running the Fortran program MCDS directly with
a command such as

"C:\Program Files\Distance6\MCDS" 0, "C:\Temp\Input File.txt"

That is the technical answer to your question. My experience has been
that for reasonable data, competing models with small delta-AIC values
produce very similar density estimates. To have small differences in
delta-AIC but large differences in estimated density is an unusual
situation and may indicate problems with the data.

On 09/05/2014 00:29, Douglas Kelt wrote:
> > Are users limited to 5 competing models when performing model-averaging in Distance? I have V 6.2 but this issue was identical in 6.0. In th Model Definition Properties I can only include a maximum of 5 models. Unfortunately, I have more than 5 models with low AIC scores and would like to run more than 5. Is this possible?
